name_reason: Descriptor 'crt_equivalent_lx_module_loader' is correct and convention-compliant (crt_equivalent_* CRT wrapper that loads an LX module). The trailing '_3647b' equals the function's own entry address (0x3647b), so by the strict no-address-residue rule it is a Ghidra address tag rather than a domain ID, which would argue for stripping it to crt_equivalent_lx_module_loader. However, the entire CRT-equivalent LX family in src/crt/crt.c uses the same address-tag convention as a stable disambiguator (crt_equivalent_lx_chunk_read_36107 @0x36107, crt_equivalent_lx_header_reader_36344 @0x36344, crt_equivalent_exit_chain_stub_36de3 @0x36de3); renaming this one in isolation would break the family's uniform naming and these siblings are referenced by call site inside this very body. Decision deferred to Stage 2 (which owns rename + protos.h/globals.h/call-site propagation and can decide the family policy as a whole). Marked uncertain rather than rename so Stage 2 makes the family-wide call.
stage2_review: rename -> crt_equivalent_lx_module_loader. Reverses the shard's keep lean (which assumed the family kept the tag): ALL 6 other crt_equivalent_* address-tagged fns (lx_chunk_read_36107, lx_header_reader_36344, exit_chain_stub_36de3, fpe_default_handler_3d26e, matherr_default_thunk_4d340, matherr_default_return_zero_4d8ea) have verdict=rename dropping the tag, so keeping _3647b would make this the lone address-tagged outlier. Family policy = drop the tag. Descriptor unique after drop.
purpose: Watcom CRT-equivalent LX/LE runtime module loader: reads the MZ->LX header, walks the object + page + fixup tables, writes the loaded image into a caller buffer (or a freshly allocated one) and applies 32-bit relocations. Dead in FD2 (static-link single-LE never invokes runtime LE loading) but re-emitted because the CLIB3S overlay/dynamic-load chain pulls in the __loadm-family obj and this body does not byte-match the public Watcom one.
logic_summary: 1) handle = (flags&1)?path-as-handle : open(path,0x200); open==-1 -> return 0. 2) total_size = crt_equivalent_lx_header_reader_36344(path,flags). 3) if flags&4: caller_buf = (*data_ail_alloc_fnptr)(total_size); null -> close(if !flags&1)+return 0; else use caller_buf. 4) memset(caller_buf,0,total_size); out_cursor=alloc_base=caller_buf. 5) read e_lfanew (MZ+0x3C, 4B) + 2B magic; strcmp vs "LX"; mismatch -> close+return 0. 6) read full 0xAC LX header into lx_header. 7) for each object (lx_header+0x44 count): read 0x18 object record; for each page (obj+0x10 count): read 0x8 page entry; on first page of a flag-3 (bit0|bit1) object with a misaligned cursor and obj_idx!=0, bump out_cursor by 0x10-(alloc_base&0xf) for 16-byte inter-object alignment; record obj_base_table[obj_idx+1]=out_cursor and page_base_table[page_count]=out_cursor; read min(obj_remaining, page byte-count) bytes from (page_data_idx<<shift)+page_data_base into out_cursor; advance out_cursor. 8) read first cumulative fixup-page offset (lx_header+0x68). 9) for each fixup page (lx_header+0x14 count): read next cumulative offset; for each fixup record in [prev,this): read src_type+target_type, validate ((src_type&7)!=0 && !((target_type&4)&&!(target_type&0x20)) && !(src_type&0x20)) else abort->close->return 0; read src_offset(2)+target_obj(1)+target_disp(2); if src_offset<=lx_header+0x28 write obj_base_table[target_obj]+target_disp at page_base_table[page]+src_offset (32-bit reloc). 10) close handle (if !flags&1); return caller_buf.

params.name: path
params.semantics: Overloaded by flags bit0: when flags&1==0 it is a null-terminated path string passed to open(); when flags&1==1 it is a caller-supplied int handle reused as an in-memory base (each chunk read becomes a memcpy). Also forwarded verbatim to crt_equivalent_lx_header_reader_36344.
params.reason: Name reflects the documented dominant role (path to open). The flags&1 handle-overload is fully documented in the comment block, so 'path' remains the clearest primary label; no address residue.

params.name: flags
params.semantics: Bit-flags controlling load mode: bit0 = use-caller-handle (skip open/close, treat path as handle), bit2 = allocate the output buffer via data_ail_alloc_fnptr (else use caller_buf). Low byte also passed to the header reader and every chunk read.

params.name: caller_buf
params.semantics: Caller-supplied output buffer for the loaded image; used only when flags&4==0. When flags&4==1 it is ignored on entry and overwritten by the alloc result. Returned (the load base) on success.
params.reason: Descriptive, matches usage, no address residue.

returns.semantics: On success returns the output buffer base (caller-supplied when flags&4==0, or the allocated buffer when flags&4==1). Returns 0 on any failure: open failure, alloc failure, LX magic mismatch, or an invalid fixup record.
